summary.intent: Investigate and fix slow unit test performance in the `cli` and `strategy` packages of the entireio/cli Go project.
summary.outcome: Reduced `cli` package test time from ~34s to ~7.8s and `strategy` package from ~20.5s to ~16.4s by backdating transcript file mtimes in test helpers and skipping `PrepareTranscript` on non-existent files during agent auto-detection. Changes merged into PR #823.

repo: Global git config has `commit.gpgsign=true` with SSH signing; system `git` CLI commands in tests pick this up even when the test repo has `gpgsign=false` set locally via go-git.
`waitForTranscriptFlush` in claudecode/lifecycle.go polls for up to 3s (`maxWait = 3 * time.Second`) when a transcript file exists and is fresh (< 2 min old), designed for live sessions.
Cursor's `PrepareTranscript` lacks the fast-path for non-existent files that Claude Code has — it polls for the full 3s even when the file will never appear.
`detectAgentByTranscript` iterates all registered agents and calls `resolveAndValidateTranscript` for each, meaning any agent with a blocking `PrepareTranscript` multiplies test latency.
`TestListSessionsFunctionsWithoutRepo` in the strategy package runs against the real repo without changing CWD, making it inherently slow (~4s) as it reads real checkpoint data.
The attach test suite uses `t.Chdir`, preventing parallelization; sequential execution means per-test latency compounds directly into total suite time.
Test helpers like `setupClaudeTranscript` create fresh transcript files which inadvertently trigger the live-session polling path in `PrepareTranscript`.

code.finding: `waitForTranscriptFlush` has a fast-path: if `os.Stat` fails (file doesn't exist), it returns immediately. But if the file exists and is fresh, it polls for up to `maxWait = 3 * time.Second`.
Cursor's `PrepareTranscript` polls for 3s even when the file doesn't exist — no fast-path on initial `os.Stat` failure, unlike Claude Code's implementation.
`PrepareTranscript` was called unconditionally before the file-existence check. Fix: move the call inside the file-exists guard so it's only invoked when the transcript file is already present.
`setupClaudeTranscript` creates transcript files with current mtime. Fix: backdate mtime by 3+ minutes so `waitForTranscriptFlush` treats them as stale and skips polling.
Both `TestSessionHasNewContent*` tests write fresh transcript files, triggering the 3s poll. Fixed by backdating mtime after write.

workflow: CPU profiling (only 60ms CPU in a 3.1s test) quickly revealed the bottleneck was I/O wait / sleep, not computation — narrowing the investigation to polling/sleep calls.
Comparing test timing across agents (Gemini: 0.06s vs Claude Code: 3s) was an effective differential diagnosis technique to isolate which agent's code path introduced the delay.
The `t.Chdir` constraint preventing test parallelization means per-test latency has a direct 1:1 impact on suite runtime — fixing individual test latency is the only lever.
GPG signing via SSH agent can silently slow down tests that shell out to `git commit` even with local repo config overrides, if the global config isn't overridden by the test environment.

friction: Three user interruptions mid-investigation required 'Continue' prompts, breaking flow during critical reasoning steps.
Multiple rounds of indirect investigation (CPU profiling, tracing, grepping for sleeps, checking hooks) before isolating the root cause to `waitForTranscriptFlush`.
go-git's `SetConfig` writes to `.git/config` correctly but the mental model that system `git` CLI would respect it caused an early false lead on GPG signing as the root cause.
Cursor's `PrepareTranscript` lacking the Claude Code fast-path was a non-obvious second source of latency discovered only after the primary fix.
GPG signing was unavailable during commit (1Password agent), requiring `--no-gpg-sign` flag.
open_items: `TestListSessionsFunctionsWithoutRepo` in the strategy package runs against the real repo without CWD isolation — should be refactored to use a temp repo, but was deferred as a separate fix.
Cursor's `PrepareTranscript` still lacks a fast-path for non-existent files; only the call site in `attach.go` was guarded. Cursor's implementation itself could be improved.
The `strategy` package still takes ~16.4s; the remaining time is dominated by legitimate git-heavy tests that weren't addressed in this session.
The attach test suite can't be parallelized due to `t.Chdir` usage — if further speedup is needed, tests would need to be refactored to avoid directory changes.
